# Refuse SharedCanvas readiness after renderer module load failure

## Context
Stage host-integration research reproduced the same failed Canvas admission in development and composed production. The [mounted observation checkpoint](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-stage/issues/32#issuecomment-6163886671) binds the inputs and loader results. A missing renderer module returns `success:false`; a module that registers its singleton and then throws also returns `success:false`, but the current host can still initialize that renderer and publish Canvas readiness.

## The Problem
`SharedCanvas.initAsync()` ignores the returned `Canvas.loadModule()` outcome. It waits for a namespace stub whether import succeeded or failed. With no stub, later offscreen registration calls `initGraph` on undefined; with a partially registered or previously available stub, failed admission can appear ready. Teardown likewise reaches a namespace renderer even when this host never initialized its graph.

The older closed `#8811`/`#8950`/`#8952` work covers transfer, loader placement and worker/stub ordering. Those dispositions do not resolve the current negative-result/foreign-graph ownership cases. Memory hits `f957de5a` and `6fec004c` preserve that history rather than establish a current repair.

## The Architectural Reality
`src/app/SharedCanvas.mjs` owns module/stub admission, graph readiness, sizing and visibility. `src/component/Canvas.mjs` owns transfer/unregister; `src/worker/Canvas.mjs` owns the structured loader result. `Base.construct()` resolves `ready()` only after `initAsync()` returns, so throwing on expected admission failure wedges that promise. Renderer namespaces are shared routing addresses, not per-host graph ownership.

Design authority: SharedCanvas's lifecycle JSDoc says it initializes the graph when offscreen canvas is ready; the observed undefined `initGraph` is a crash, and publishing Canvas ready after an explicit import refusal contradicts that lifecycle.

## The Fix
Consume the existing loader outcome before admitting graph work. Use an internal per-host admission/owned-graph guard and the existing `isCanvasReady` config; do not add a second writable readiness authority. Expected failure settles live host initialization normally and emits an addressed `canvasLoadFailed` notification. Skip transfer/graph/theme/resize work for refused hosts; unregister only their own transferred canvas if a race already transferred it. Clear only a graph this host actually started, with its captured renderer/window. Fence continuations against destruction and stale captured window identity. Preserve successful delayed-stub and preloaded/no-import-path hosts.

Prescription checked: `src/app/SharedCanvas.mjs` owns this concern. The ordinary Canvas loader keeps its current return contract. New focused tests belong beside `SharedCanvasVisibility.spec.mjs`; the mounted Stage fixture supplies the real consumer falsifier.

## Contract Ledger
| Target surface | Authority | Result / fallback | Docs and evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Canvas.loadModule()` → `SharedCanvas.initAsync()` | Existing `{success,path,error}` writer in `src/worker/Canvas.mjs` | Negative or rejected load never admits renderer work; live host `ready()` settles | Loader/host JSDoc; failed-without-stub and failed-with-stub controls |
| `isCanvasReady` / `canvasReady` | SharedCanvas graph-init boundary | Publish only for successful admission and this live host's graph; preloaded hosts retained | Existing config/event JSDoc; delayed-success and mounted controls |
| `canvasLoadFailed` | SharedCanvas's per-host admission failure | One addressed event with host, renderer, configured path and categorical reason; listener failure cannot wedge initialization | New event JSDoc; event/ready settlement assertions |
| Transfer, teardown and sizing | Component Canvas maps + SharedCanvas owned-graph boundary | Refused or retired host never clears another renderer; own transfer/graph retired once | Lifecycle JSDoc; close-during-load and surviving-renderer browser control |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Actual negative load with no stub and with a pre-existing/partially registered stub settles live host `ready()`, emits one failure event, and makes zero `initGraph`/`canvasReady`/theme/resize calls.
- [ ] Worker-start/rejected-loader/bounded-missing-stub failures settle without an unhandled rejection; destruction/stale-window continuations publish no readiness or failure event.
- [ ] Successful delayed-stub and preloaded/no-import-path hosts retain normal graph, theme, size and visibility behavior.
- [ ] Closing a refused host retires only its transferred canvas; a healthy renderer continues painting with its registration and measured resources intact.
- [ ] Focused lifecycle units, the existing owning unit checks and full units pass; mounted development and composed-production controls prove the original negative-result readiness failure is removed.
- [ ] Stage research consumes the exact repaired Engine head separately from the installed candidate and records the final remaining bounds.

## Out of Scope
Automatic retries, new loader roots/manifests, installed bundle or runtime-extension activation, Base readiness redesign, Sparkline's independent initializer, renderer shader/partial-allocation repair and generic GPU memory reclamation.

## Avoided Traps
A namespace stub as admission proof; throwing an expected failure and stranding `Base.ready()`; clearing a shared renderer the failed host never owned; a second mutable load-status config; claiming the independent Sparkline path fixed.

Decision Record impact: none — correction at the existing SharedCanvas lifecycle owner, no extension-host approval.
Structure map: N/A — Body primitive plus an established sibling test directory.
